grammar.example: The keys are on the table. The cat is under the bed.

grammar.structure: next to / between / behind / in front of
grammar.example: The lamp is next to the sofa.
It's in the drawer. They're on the shelf.
I need a table. I don't need a TV.

tips.en: "On" is for surfaces (on the table, on the wall), "in" is for inside something (in the box, in the drawer).
tips.es: «On» es para superficies (on the table, on the wall) e «in» para dentro de algo (in the box, in the drawer).

tips.en: "Furniture" is uncountable: "some furniture" or "a piece of furniture", never "furnitures".
tips.es: «Furniture» (muebles) es incontable: «some furniture» o «a piece of furniture», nunca «furnitures».

tips.en: "Glasses" (lentes) is always plural: "Where are my glasses?"
tips.es: «Glasses» (lentes) siempre va en plural: «Where are my glasses?»

tips.en: "Closet" is a small room or cabinet for clothes. In British English it's often "wardrobe".
tips.es: «Closet» es el armario o vestidor. En inglés británico se suele decir «wardrobe».

tips.en: Used furniture is cheap at "yard sales" and "thrift stores" in the US.
tips.es: En Estados Unidos los muebles usados son baratos en las «yard sales» (ventas de garaje) y las «thrift stores».

story.title: Moving Day
story.text: Today is moving day! Carmen has her new apartment. Mike and Leo help her with the furniture. "Where do you want the sofa, Mom?" asks Mike. "In front of the window, please." Mike and Leo carry the sofa. "It's too heavy!" says Leo. Next to the sofa there is a small table and a lamp. In the bedroom, the bed is between two windows, and there is a big mirror behind the door. "Grandma, where are your glasses?" asks Leo. Carmen looks on the table, in her bag, under the chair… Leo laughs. "They're on your head!" Everybody laughs. At the end of the day, the apartment is a little crowded, but it looks great. Carmen makes coffee in her new kitchen. Her first coffee at home.
story.es: ¡Hoy es el día de la mudanza! Carmen ya tiene su nuevo departamento. Mike y Leo la ayudan con los muebles. «¿Dónde quieres el sofá, suegra?», pregunta Mike. «Frente a la ventana, por favor.» Mike y Leo cargan el sofá. «¡Pesa demasiado!», dice Leo. Al lado del sofá hay una mesita y una lámpara. En el dormitorio, la cama está entre dos ventanas y hay un espejo grande detrás de la puerta. «Abuela, ¿dónde están tus lentes?», pregunta Leo. Carmen busca en la mesa, en su bolsa, debajo de la silla… Leo se ríe. «¡Los tienes en la cabeza!» Todos se ríen. Al final del día, el departamento está un poco lleno, pero se ve genial. Carmen prepara café en su nueva cocina. Su primer café en casa.
